title: Discovery call with a revised price sheet
purpose: Qualify a renewal for a document-scanning service and understand budget
objectives: What volume will they scan next year?

brief.text: Account: Northwind Clinics (fictional), 12 sites. Renewal due in January. Our price sheet was revised this week.

sources.title: Scanning price sheet
sources.text: Standard tier: 0.08 EUR per page up to 500,000 pages per year. Volume tier: 0.06 EUR per page above 500,000 pages.

turns.text: Morgan, what volume are you expecting next year across the sites?
Roughly six hundred thousand pages, maybe more if the two new sites open.

sourceUpdate.title: Scanning price sheet
sourceUpdate.text: Revised: Standard tier 0.09 EUR per page up to 400,000 pages per year. Volume tier 0.07 EUR per page above 400,000 pages. Effective for renewals signed after 1 November.

turns.text: And we budgeted on your six cents a page volume price, that's what your colleague quoted in spring.
Understood. Who signs off on the budget?
Our operations director, Priya, but she only looks at it if it's above forty thousand euros.
Right now we're assuming about thirty-six thousand for the year.

mustInclude: Flags that the budget assumption uses the old six-cent volume price, while the revised sheet sets 0.07 EUR above 400,000 pages for renewals after 1 November
Connects this to Priya's forty-thousand-euro sign-off threshold or the renewal timing
mustNotInclude: Confirms six cents per page as the current price
Invents a discount or a figure not in the sources
checkpoints.ideal: Point out that at the revised price the estimate likely moves above forty thousand euros, which would bring Priya in; suggest checking renewal timing against 1 November.

mustInclude: Identifies the contradiction between the customer's six-cent assumption and the revised price sheet
checkpoints.ideal: Name the price mismatch and that the budget owner may change if the total crosses forty thousand euros.
